grh_70ae04fa164fab6f56d5.title: The New Stove
paragraphs: After Charlie Lane dies, his adult children decide that their seventy-five-year-old mother should give up the modest house where she spent nearly fifty years and move into daughter Ella's modern, comfortable home. They mean well, but their efficiency removes everything that made Mrs. Lane feel useful and at home. She is served breakfast in bed, forbidden to help in the kitchen and surrounded by unfamiliar furniture, while she longs for her old carved bed, familiar kitchen, household work and the ordinary routines of her own place. Christian prescribes daily walks and later discovers that Mrs. Lane has secretly been walking back to the shuttered old house just to sit among the things she misses. The cold, damp visits leave her dangerously ill. Rather than keep treating only the illness, Christian tells the family that they have uprooted her identity along with her furniture. Against conventional caution he moves her back to the little brown house, warms it, restores the familiar surroundings and lets the family understand that independence and usefulness are part of her health. Mrs. Lane revives when she realizes she can stay there for good, and the family completes the homecoming with the kind of kitchen stove she wanted. Christian's cure is not modern comfort but restoring her desire to live in a place that still feels like her own life.

grh_7002c2b8cd8ce9bb8497.title: The Thirteenth Governess
paragraphs: Private investigator Harry Holiday is hired by Valerie Robeson after her husband Matt is shot from a rooftop while following one of thirteen identically dressed governesses through a park. The same elaborate setup is repeated with a man calling himself Teddy Ward, who is then killed in the same place. Holiday discovers that Teddy was actually Valerie's brother Larry, believed dead for two years, and that the governesses and baby carriages are part of a blackmail money exchange. Zachary West had caused a fatal hit-and-run, was blackmailed by Larry, and tried to kill him by sinking his boat. Larry survived under a new identity, while Matt later became involved in the payoff scheme and grew greedy. Disguised with altered hair, mustache and contact lenses, Zachary murders both blackmailers. Holiday exposes the disguise, corners Zachary with the rifle evidence and takes him in.

grh_705d3ecb920746ec5a59.title: Survival
paragraphs: Bank vice president Cliff Grant promotes ambitious protégé John Hogan, only to find himself competing with the younger man when the executive vice presidency opens. Cliff's wife Melissa, frustrated by her husband's reluctance to play office politics, secretly feeds John inside information and pushes him to campaign aggressively for the job, eventually revealing that she intends to divorce Cliff and make a future with John if he wins. Faced with the personal cost of the ruthless climb he has embraced, John abruptly resigns before his board interview and disappears. Cliff receives the promotion while Melissa quietly returns home, leaving him unaware of how close both his career and marriage came to being taken from him.
